what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A breakfast BBC page became a vault and site
sections.para: The BBC live page on two PHP flaws led, within four hours, to an evidence vault created at 08:03 UTC, a section here at 08:13 and a dedicated site at 09:27. By 12:05 the vault held 184 sources and 177 dated captures from six writers.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Capture first; several agents, one vault, the record kept
sections.para: Pages change by the hour, so the vault came before the page, with captures only ever added and one file per writer. The figures were pinned to what they measure, the agencies' disagreement made visible, and forty sources nearly lost to uncommitted work were recovered.

sections.label: What I was reading at breakfast
sections.line: The reporting had numbers that did not add up
sections.para: The BBC page from 06:16 UTC reported agencies advising sites offline, and a 70% of the internet figure the BBC could not verify beside 30 million websites. The real question was the blast radius: what is on each server and what stands in front of it.

sections.label: Capture before you write
sections.line: The vault was created before there was a page
sections.para: The vault came first at 08:03 because live pages, down pages and posts change within hours. The capture tool keeps six things per capture, each hashed, and the BBC page's second capture already held a post the first did not.

sections.label: A section in ten minutes, and agents by beat
sections.line: A section at 08:13 and four agents by beat
sections.para: The section went out with one source, a status per claim and the captures listed by hash, not republished. Four agents collected primary sources, researchers, governments and news, and the protocol moved to one file per writer to avoid conflicts.

sections.label: Following the link someone sends
sections.line: A sent link became a bundled repository, counted
sections.para: The NCSC-NL php2shell repository was kept whole as a git bundle with its 52 commits, and its inventory parsed: 674 products at commit cca173c64ec5, 206 Vulnerable. It also gave the CVE numbers, the fixed releases and the first agency disagreement.

sections.label: The numbers, pinned to what they measure
sections.line: The scale figures measure different things
sections.para: 70% is a headline; the body says 70% of websites, a language share. Other counts are 2.6 million hosts and about 6,000 resources in Latvia. Exploitation claims were attempts and probes, and agencies differ on taking systems offline.

sections.label: What went wrong
sections.line: Two agents stopped before committing their captures
sections.para: One agent's pull showed 224 conflicts, 223 identical. Two agents left forty sources uncommitted, including French prefecture maintenance pages captured at 08:19. They were recovered, and two rules follow: commit after every source, and check every clone.

sections.label: A site of its own
sections.line: A dedicated site now holds the facts
sections.para: php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai, released at 09:27 and at v0.2.2 by noon, reads the same vault with briefings per role. The section here will move to it and retire, leaving a pointer; the newsroom keeps context and opinion.

sections.label: Where things stand
sections.para: At 12:05 UTC the vault held 184 sources, 177 captures and 855 hashed files, with 61 claims and 67 events. Hashes show bytes unchanged since publication, not when captured. Next come exposure, exploitation over time and evidence-backed steps.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: One morning, agents' work, private evidence, no advice
sections.para: The times are one newsroom's; the vault is private, so readers cannot check captures yet; nothing is anchored; the figures are as sources state them; agents can be wrong; nothing here is patch advice.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: A conversation, two memos, captured sources, counted
sections.para: The origin is Dinis's conversation with the agent and two memos. Sources are the BBC live page, the NCSC-NL repository and the php.net advisory, all captured. The counts come from the vault's source, provenance, claims and timeline files at 12:05 UTC.
